Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 37, verse 1–4:

Name of the Surah

• It is called al-Saffat (Those Who Set in Ranks), because it opens with Allah's oath by al-Saffat, namely the noble angels.

Among the Objectives of the Surah

• Affirming the oneness of Allah, the Exalted, and presenting the many proofs of His sole creation of the great creatures, such as the heavenly and earthly worlds and what is in them.

• Mentioning some of the positions of the polytheists, such as their denial of the Resurrection (al-Ba'th), their accusation of the Messenger (ﷺ) of sorcery, and their meeting of his call with mockery and derision.

• Affirming the Resurrection and what follows it of recompense, describing the state of the polytheists on that Day, the painful punishment prepared for them, describing the bliss of the believers and what has been prepared for them of good food, drink, and spouses.

• Presenting the stories of the messengers with their peoples, how Allah helped His messengers, raised their status, and blessed them, and describing what befell the nations that denied the messengers.

• Explaining the corruption of the polytheists' beliefs about divinity, their attributing partners to Allah, and their claim that the angels are the daughters of Allah, and explaining the rank and reality of the angels.

[Tafsir]

Allah swears by the angels who, in their worship, stand in tightly arranged rows, and by the angels who drive the clouds and guide them by the command of Allah, and by the angels who recite the remembrance of Allah and His speech, exalted is He. Indeed, your God, O people, is One, with no partner, so devote your worship and obedience to Him alone. Allah swears by whatever He wills of His creation, but a created being may not swear except by Allah, for swearing by other than Allah is shirk.
